name: Vinny Table
subtitle: Plan-derived corner-leg dining table
description: A parametric 1:10 solid-oak model of the 96 × 40 inch Vinny dining table, with grouped direct dimensions, rounded leg edges, square apron joinery lands, an outer-only apron roundover, optional wood stretchers or steel C-channels, four calculated-angle diagonal corner blocks, and independent leveling feet.

dimensionTargets: The default tabletop is 96 in long by 40 in wide by 1 1/2 in thick and the finished table is 30 in high.
The default advanced flush base uses eight 1 1/2 in thick profiled leg halves, mitered in pairs into four L-shaped corner legs.
Each advanced leg profile is 6 in wide at the frame, meets the live apron bottom with a 1 1/2 in circular shoulder, and tapers to a 2 in foot.

The default aprons and wood stretchers are 1 1/2 in thick by 2 1/2 in high; apron lengths derive from the live table and leg widths, while stretcher and channel lengths derive from the live inside apron faces.
Three cross stretchers use the centerline plus two positions 22 in on center from it.
The alternate cross-support system replaces the three wood stretchers with three steel C-channels on the same centerlines.
Four diagonal corner blocks meet the square inside faces of the long and short aprons with end angles calculated from independent long-side and short-side reaches.

The tabletop uses a 1 in plan-corner radius and 1/2 in top-edge roundover; the leg outside corner uses an independent 3/4 in radius while all other exposed convex vertical edges share a 1/8 in radius.
Only the outer lower edge of each apron uses the 3/4 in roundover; the inner lower edge and both end lands remain square and flush.
The flush top uses a 1/2 in wide by 1/4 in deep perimeter shadow groove; the alternate top uses a default 1 1/2 in overhang.
The documented simple and intermediate alternatives use 2 1/2 in leg blanks and share the same editable apron dimensions.
invariants: Keep full-size dimensions independent from the mock scale denominator.
Derive every apron, stretcher, and channel length directly from the editable table, leg, and apron dimensions; expose no deduction parameters.
Keep the advanced corner legs as continuous closed L-shaped solids whose circular shoulders meet the live apron bottom exactly.
Keep the simple, intermediate, and advanced leg options registered to the same base and tabletop envelope.
Keep the flush shadow groove and overhang option mutually exclusive and derived from the selected top style.
Keep the tabletop, four legs, four aprons, selected cross supports, and four optional diagonal corner blocks as closed printable solids.

Keep tabletop corners, tabletop edge roundover, the independent outside leg radius, the shared radius on every other exposed convex leg edge, and the apron outer-bottom roundover independently editable and fabrication-visible.
Keep apron end lands and the entire apron inside face square so the leg and calculated-angle diagonal blocks trim flush without a rounded gap.
Keep steel C-channels in hardware geometry and exports; never merge them into the oak STL or credit them as apron-leg racking braces.
Keep the four independent leveling feet on Z = 0 and shorten the wood while preserving overall table height.
Keep oak grain aligned lengthwise on the tabletop and long aprons, crosswise on short members, and vertically on legs.
Treat the source PDF as supplemental dimensional guidance and omit construction details that are not dimensioned.
Treat the structural panel as a geometry-only comparison and require full-size joint, racking, rocking, deflection, and repeated-load tests before build approval.
Export registered support-free wood and hardware STLs while leveling feet are enabled; disabling them restores direct wood floor contact.
